---
format:
  typst:
    font-paths: resources/fonts
execute:
  warning: false
  echo: false
  message: false
  eval: true
---

```{=typst}
// === PAGE ===
#set page(
  paper: "a4",
  fill: rgb("#F8F7F0"),
  margin: (top: 0.5in, bottom: 0.5in, left: 0.6in, right: 0.6in),
  footer: context {
    set text(size: 8pt, fill: rgb("#666"), style: "italic")
    let updated = datetime.today().display(
      "Updated [month repr:long] [day padding:none], [year]"
    )
    // one page, so no page count
    grid(
      columns: (1fr, 1fr),
      align(left)[#updated],
      align(right)[#link("https://pingfan.org")[pingfan.org]],
    )
  },
)

#set text(font: ("Optima", "Helvetica Neue", "Arial"), size: 10pt)
#set par(leading: 0.62em, justify: false, spacing: 0pt)
#set block(spacing: 0pt)

// === SPACING KNOBS ===
// `gap` controls every major boundary (above sections, below section rules,
// between lists/tables/entries). Tune this one value to tighten or loosen
// the whole resume. `entry-gap` is the tighter gap from an entry title to
// its first bullet.
#let gap = 7pt
#let entry-gap = 3pt

// === LISTS & TABLES ===
#show list: set block(spacing: 0.25em)
// a bullet is a short gray hairline, a number gray Maple Mono with its
// period, as on the site
#let list-mark = box(height: 0.66em, width: 0.5em, place(horizon, line(length: 0.5em, stroke: 0.6pt + rgb("#A3A096"))))
#let enum-mark(n) = text(font: "Maple Mono NF", size: 0.8em, fill: rgb("#77746B"))[#n.]
#set list(indent: 1em, body-indent: 0.4em, marker: list-mark)

// Lists/tables emit `gap` AFTER themselves so the gap to the next block is
// always `gap`. Tables also get a small lead-in for breathing room.
#show list: it => { it; v(gap) }
#show table: it => { v(3pt); it; v(gap) }

// Navy-blue links
#show link: set text(fill: rgb(0%, 20%, 60%))

// === HELPERS ===
// A mark from the site's glyph map (resources/styles/styles.scss), read at
// compile time so the documents and the page share one drawing: gray, at
// the size of the text, its center 0.29em above the baseline, between the
// lowercase and capital centers, as the page's marks and the skill marks.
#let glyph(name, size: 0.9em) = {
  let scss = read("resources/styles/styles.scss")
  let svg = scss.match(regex("\n  \"" + name + "\": \"(<svg[^\"]*</svg>)\"")).captures.at(0)
  box(width: size, height: 0.58em, place(horizon + center, image(bytes(svg.replace("'black'", "'#77746B'")), height: size)))
}

// Section header with underline rule.
#let hair = rgb("#BDBAB0")
#let muted = rgb("#77746B")
#let section(name) = {
  text(size: 11pt, weight: "bold", tracking: 0.05em)[#upper[#name]]
  v(4pt)
  line(length: 100%, stroke: 0.5pt + hair)
  v(gap)
}

// Dates and places, quiet and in tabular figures.
#let aside(body) = text(weight: "regular", fill: muted, number-width: "tabular")[#body]

// Project/general entry — title left, dates right.
#let entry(title, dates) = {
  grid(
    columns: (1fr, auto),
    align: (left, right),
    title, aside(dates),
  )
  v(entry-gap)
}

// Work entry — fixed-width left column so locations line up across rows.
#let work-entry(company-role, location, dates) = {
  grid(
    columns: (55%, 1fr, auto),
    align: (left, left, right),
    company-role,
    aside(location),
    aside(dates),
  )
  v(entry-gap)
}

// === HEADER ===
#align(center)[
  #text(size: 20pt, weight: "bold")[Pingfan Hu]
]

#v(8pt)

// the contact line: a mark before each item, a hairline between items, as
// in the skills block
#let sep = [#h(0.8em)#box(height: 0.58em, place(horizon, line(angle: 90deg, length: 0.7em, stroke: 0.4pt + hair)))#h(0.8em)]
#align(center)[
  #text(size: 9pt)[
    #glyph("map-pin")~Greater Melbourne, Australia
    #sep
    #glyph("mail")~#link("mailto:pingfanhu@proton.me")[pingfanhu\@proton.me]
    #sep
    #glyph("phone")~+61 431 251 227
    #sep
    #glyph("compass")~#link("https://pingfan.org")[pingfan.org]
  ]
]

#v(9pt)

#section[Education]

#align(center)[
  #table(
    columns: (auto, auto, auto, auto, auto),
    stroke: none,
    inset: (x: 0pt, y: 1.5pt),
    column-gutter: 14pt,
    align: left,
    aside[2026], [George Washington University], [Ph.D. (defended)], [Systems Engineering], [GPA 4.0],
    aside[2018], [University of Sydney], [M.P.E.], [Mechanical Engineering], [GPA 3.5],
    aside[2015], [Pennsylvania State University], [B.S.], [Industrial Engineering], [GPA 3.2],
  )
]

#section[Skills]
```

```{r}
#| results: asis
# the About page's skills in two columns, each group a label over a hairline
# with its skills running on beneath; see the script
source(here::here("resources/scripts/skills.R"))
cat(skills_typst("flow", cols = 2))
```

```{=typst}
#section[#link("https://pingfan.org/research")[#text(fill: black)[Research & Software]]]

#entry[*#link("https://emaki.lol")[Emaki]* - _Agentic Development Environment, Alkaline Software_][2026 - Present]

- Lead developer of Emaki, a desktop app that supports agentic workflows, built in Rust with GPUI for macOS, Windows, and Linux.

#entry[*surveydown* - _Open-Source Survey Platform of the Helveston Lab at GWU_][2024 - 2026]

- Built surveydown, an open-source R package for programmable, reproducible surveys on Quarto, Shiny, and PostgreSQL: 180+ GitHub stars, 11,000+ CRAN downloads.
- Built sdstudio, its GUI for survey preview and database management: 2,500+ CRAN downloads.
- First-author paper in _PLOS One_; 2nd prize at the GW Open Source Awards; profiled by GW Engineering.
- Presented at posit::conf, US-RSE, GW OSCON 2025, and GW OSCON 2026.

#entry[*BEV Smart Charging Economies* - _Joint Project of GWU, UC Davis & UC Irvine_][2023 - 2026]

- Consumer side: fielded a national survey of 1,300+ U.S. BEV owners via Meta and Dynata, and estimated mixed logit models of preferences for smart charging program attributes.
- Grid side: simulated 10,000 BEVs on NHTS travel patterns against CAISO and NYISO net load; swept 5 TOU windows and 11 enrollment levels to quantify peak shaving and cost efficiency.
- Published two first-author papers (_Environmental Research Letters_, _IEEE VPPC_); a third is under review.
- Presented at TRB 2024 and the GW 2026 R&D Showcase.

#section[Work Experience]

#work-entry[*Alkaline Software* - _Co-Founder_][#glyph("map-pin")~Remote][2026 - Present]

- Co-founded an app development studio with Professor John Helveston. We are two data scientists building open-source apps that benefit our own team and the community.

#work-entry[*George Washington University* - _Graduate Research Assistant_][#glyph("map-pin")~DC, USA][2023 - Present]

- Conducted the research and built the software listed under Research & Software above.
- Build reproducible Claude Code workflows with plugins, skills, MCPs, and hooks; taught a GW TAI workshop.
- Teaching assistant for the advisor's data science courses: group lectures, project advising, and grading.

#work-entry[*Harsco Rail* - _Software Engineer_][#glyph("map-pin")~SC, USA & Beijing, China][2021 - 2022]

- Led C++ and CAN bus software for rail maintenance machines across USA and China. Obtained 25 total releases.

#work-entry[*GE Appliances* - _Project Engineer_][#glyph("map-pin")~Qingdao, China][2019 - 2020]

- Managed 500+ components across 9 washing machine models from development to production.

#work-entry[*Kurtz Ersa GmbH* - _Assistant Process Engineer (Intern)_][#glyph("map-pin")~Wertheim, Germany][2017]

- Led a 2-month Design of Experiments on new soldering technology across 200 PCB samples.
```
